moments.name: 10.Nd5
moments.headline: 10.Nd5! The only good move here: every alternative is clearly worse.
points: The next best move, 10.Be3, would drop White's winning chances from 66% to 53% (+0.29).

Black answers 10…Nxd5, taking the knight on d5.

moments.name: 18.Bb5
moments.headline: 18.Bb5!! A real sacrifice: White gives up material and the engine still rates it best.
points: Puts the bishop on b5 where it can be taken.
Black can take, but after 18…axb5 19.Rxa8 Be7 20.Kc1 the engine rates it +0.51.
18.Bb5 wins the exchange, picking it up with 19.Rxa8, and threatens Bxc6+, winning the queen for a bishop.

It threatens Bxc6+, winning the queen for a bishop, so Black has to spend the next move on it.
Black answers 18…axb5, taking the bishop on b5 and uncovering an attack on the rook on a1, leaving White with no bishop pair.

why.title: The idea
why.text: 18.Bb5!! offers the bishop on b5. Taking it gives White the material back and more.

why.title: What White gives up
why.text: 18.Bb5 puts the bishop on b5 where it can be taken by the a6 pawn and the queen on c6. That's a bishop on offer.

why.title: What it does instead
why.text: It threatens Bxc6+, winning the queen for a bishop.

why.title: If Black takes the bishop
why.text: 18…axb5 is met by 19.Rxa8, taking the rook on a8 and threatening fxe5, winning a pawn. Then 22.fxe5 takes the e5 pawn, and 23.Bxe7 takes the bishop on e7. White ends up two pawns ahead: White holds the balance (+0.30). This is Black's best try.

moments.name: 18…axb5
moments.headline: 18…axb5!! A real sacrifice: Black gives up material and the engine still rates it best.
points: Leaves the rook on a8 where it can be taken.
White can take, but after 19.Rxa8 Be7 20.Kc1 f6 the engine rates it +0.41.
Takes the bishop on b5.
Moving away uncovers the rook on a8, which now hits the rook on a1.
18…axb5 threatens …Qd5+, with a dangerous check, and stops Bxc6+.
It threatens …Qd5+, with a dangerous check, so White has to spend the next move on it.

why.title: The idea
why.text: 18…axb5!! leaves the rook on a8 hanging. Taking it still leaves Black level.

why.title: What Black gives up
why.text: 18…axb5 leaves the rook on a8 hanging to the rook on a1. That's a whole rook on offer.

why.title: What it does instead
why.text: It takes the bishop on b5. White has no bishop left to guard the light squares around the king (d1, d3).

why.title: If White takes the rook
why.text: 19.Rxa8 is met by 19…Be7, clearing the way to castle kingside. Then 22…Qxf3 takes the queen on f3, and 23…dxe5 takes the e5 pawn. Black is a piece down: Black holds the balance (+0.49). This is White's best try.

why.title: Without the sacrifice
why.text: The best move without the sacrifice, 18…Qxb5, is clearly weaker (+1.33 against +0.41). White answers 19.Qxb5+, taking the queen on b5 with check. That would leave Black a little worse.

moments.name: 19…Be7
moments.headline: 19…Be7! The only good move here: every alternative is clearly worse.
points: Clears the last piece between king and rook: castling kingside is now possible.
The next best move, 19…b6, would drop Black's winning chances from 46% to 31% (+2.11).
19…Be7 stops fxe5.
White was threatening fxe5, winning a pawn. Be7 takes care of it.
White answers 20.Kc1.
After 20.Kc1 f6 21.Bb4 Kf7 22.fxe5 dxe5 23.Bxe7 Kxe7 24.Rd1, the bishops are traded (+0.30).

points: Makes an escape square for the king, so back-rank checks lose their sting.

Black answers 30…Qxh2, winning a pawn.

points: The queen forks the king and the rook: both can't be saved at once.
